Descriptive summary for continuous variables

Source: R/ks_summary.r
ks_summary.Rd

Computes n, mean, SD, CV, median, Q1, Q3, min, max by group. Optionally adds a p-value for change from zero (paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank, chosen by Shapiro-Wilk normality test).

Usage

ks_summary(
  data,
  var,
  ...,
  na.rm = TRUE,
  p.change = FALSE,
  extras = NULL,
  numdec = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble.

var

Unquoted name of the numeric variable to summarise.

...

Unquoted grouping variables. Must come before na.rm, p.change, extras, and numdec in the call, which are keyword-only arguments (they must always be named).

na.rm

Logical; remove NAs before computing. Default TRUE.

p.change

Logical; if TRUE, append a p.chg column (p-value for paired change, chosen by normality). Default FALSE.

extras

An optional named list of functions for additional per-group statistics. Each function is called as f(x, na.rm = na.rm) where x is the numeric vector of var for that group. Each function must return a single scalar value. The list names become column names in the result.

Example: extras = list(mad = stats::mad, sem = function(x, na.rm) sd(x, na.rm = na.rm) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(x))))

Names that clash with built-in columns (n, mean, sd, cv, median, q1, q3, min, max, p.chg, NUMDEC) will raise an error.

numdec

Logical; if TRUE (the default), append a NUMDEC column giving the maximum number of decimal places observed in var within each group (via ks_get_numdec logic, capped at 4). Set to FALSE to suppress.

Value

A tibble with one row per group and columns n, mean, sd, median, q1, q3, min, max, any extras columns, cv, (if numdec = TRUE) NUMDEC, and (if p.change = TRUE) p.chg.

Details

Q1 and Q3 use ks_q1 / ks_q3, whose type argument defaults to getOption("kstools.quantile.type", 2L) (SAS-compatible). Set that option in .Rprofile to change the algorithm globally.

See also

ks_q1, ks_q3, ks_get_numdec

Examples

d <- data.frame(
  grp = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 10),
  val = c(rnorm(10, 5), rnorm(10, 8))
)
ks_summary(d, val, grp)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 11
#>   grp       n  mean    sd median    q1    q3   min   max    cv NUMDEC
#>   <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>  <int>
#> 1 A        10  5.21 0.912   5.27  4.50  5.82  3.95  6.56  17.5      4
#> 2 B        10  8.02 1.11    8.07  6.93  8.93  6.38  9.50  13.9      4

## Without NUMDEC
ks_summary(d, val, grp, numdec = FALSE)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 10
#>   grp       n  mean    sd median    q1    q3   min   max    cv
#>   <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 A        10  5.21 0.912   5.27  4.50  5.82  3.95  6.56  17.5
#> 2 B        10  8.02 1.11    8.07  6.93  8.93  6.38  9.50  13.9

## With extra statistics
ks_summary(d, val, grp,
  extras = list(
    mad = stats::mad,
    sem = function(x, na.rm) sd(x, na.rm = na.rm) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(x)))
  )
)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 13
#>   grp       n  mean    sd median    q1    q3   min   max   mad   sem    cv
#>   <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 A        10  5.21 0.912   5.27  4.50  5.82  3.95  6.56  1.04 0.288  17.5
#> 2 B        10  8.02 1.11    8.07  6.93  8.93  6.38  9.50  1.46 0.352  13.9
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: NUMDEC <int>
